EVACUATION ON WATER
The aircraft is equipped with 25-MAN/
30-MAN LIFE RAFTS, stowed in ceiling
compartments, inside the main cabin.
These compartments, placarded "LIFE
RAFT",
, are adjacent to each EMER-
GENCY
(MAIN
CABIN ENTRY/EXIT)
DOOR.
ESCAPE ROPES:
Overwing escape ropes are contained in the overhead liferaft compartments adjacent to
doors L3 and R3. The compartments are labeled to identify rope locations.
One end of each rope is permanently secured to the airplane structure. The opposite end is
equipped with a snap fastener. This fastener is pulled out onto the wing and is attached to
a bracket located between the inboard and outboard engines. The rope will aid personnel
in maintaining footing while moving outboard on the wing to the LIFE RAFTS. The rope
level is such that children may grasp it without difficulty, while traversing the wing,
during ditching. These ropes could also be used for emergency land evacuation.
DOOR NO. 3
STRUCTURE
LIFE RAFT INFLATION
Aft door
assist handle.
Each 25/30 MAN LIFE RAFT weighs approximately 120 Ibs. and
should be removed from the ceiling compartment by two able-bodied
persons; positioned near an EMERGENCY (MAIN CABIN ENTRY/EXIT)
DOOR and secured to the aircraft prior to launching.
1. Pull compartment door release latch
and allow door to swing open.
2. Unfasten restraining buckles/straps
secured around LIFE RAFT. Grab WHITE
assist straps on side of LIFE RAFT and
lower to floor. Close ceiling compartment.
WARNING!
DO NOT INFLATE LIFE RAFT
INSIDE AIRCRAFT
A. Position LIFE RAFT at EMERGENCY (MAIN CABIN ENTRY/EXIT) DOOR with RED
flap upward. Unsnap RED flap and secure lanyard snaphook to forward door assist
handle / seat leg / fastened seat belt, or exposed door hinge nearest the EXIT door
threshold, at ALL doors EXCEPT #L4 and #R4. At these doors attach the lanyard to
the aft door assist handle.
Forward door
assist handle.
B. After opening door, place LIFE RAFT on EXIT door threshold. Grasp inflation han-
dle and pull hard as you push LIFE RAFT out of aircraft. The initial pull on the infla.
tion handle expells the raft from its case; a secondary pull will discharge the infla-
tion bottles and the raft will inflate in approximately 15 seconds.

WELCOME ABOARD!
The Flying Tiger Line has taken every precaution to ensure your
safety during this flight and although we do not anticipate any
emergencies, this short brochure has been prepared for your
safety. We would appreciate it if you would take the time to read
this brochure and familiarize yourself with the safety features on
board our aircraft, then sit back, relax, and enjoy the flight.
- PLEASE DO NOT REMOVE FROM AIRCRAFT-

LIFE VEST
1. Individual life vest is in a
pouch under seat. Pull RED tab
marked
LIFE VEST
and remove vest from pouch.
2. Insert the arms
through the strap
loops and pull jacket
over head.
WARNING!
DO NOT INFLATE LIFE VEST
INSIDE AIRCRAFT
5. Inflate by pulling
down sharply on the
two plastic tabs.
6. To inflate orally blow into
mouthpiece.
INFANT LIFE VEST
1. The infant life vests are
stowed in an inboard ceiling
compartment, that is placarded
"INFANT LIFE VESTS."
2. Open vest.
Slip jacket over
3. Bring pull straps from
back and snap "D" rings
into snap hooks. Pull
straps until vest is snug.
4. Tie neck
strap.
3. Pull straps down
until back flap
is fully extended.
4. Tighten straps by
pulling the two PULL TABS
in an outward motion
The adult life vest is equipped with a
whistle for signaling and alerting.
SURVIVOR LOCATOR LIGHT
A light located on the shoulder
of each Life Vest is illuminated
by a water-activated battery
mounted just above the harness
buckles. At night pull ORANGE
FLAP marked "PULL TO LIGHT"
and remove plastic plugs attached
to battery. The light will illuminate
when battery submerges in water.
The infant vest is
provided with a life line
held by retaining loops in
front of the life vest. The
lifeline can be removed
from the retaining loops
and the free end attached
to an adult, life raft or
other secure object.
5. Inflate by pulling RED
toggle sharply downward.
To inflate orally blow
into mouthpiece.

EMERGENCY EXITS
Our aircraft is fully equipped with exits and facilities for
emergency evacuation as illustrated in the diagrams below. All
EMERGENCY (MAIN CABIN ENTRY/EXIT) DOORS and the UPPER
DECK (CREW SERVICE) DOOR are placarded with instructions
for their use and provided with inflatable escape slides, for
emergency evacuation. The EMERGENCY (MAIN CABIN
ENTRY/EXIT) DOORS (A) are the primary means of evacuation.
The UPPER DECK (CREW SERVICE) DOOR (B) is a secondary
evacuation route only.

NO SMOKING

Fasten

Seat back up

NO SMOKING
1.OXYGEN MASK LOCATION
Oxygen masks are stored in a compart-
ment above each row of passenger
seats. Should oxygen be required, the
compartment door will open
automatically and oxygen masks will
drop down.
2. USING THE MASK
Should oxygen masks appear, remain
seated. Grasp nearest mask and put to
your face. A short cord attached to the
outlet valve actuation pin opens the
valve and allows oxygen to flow. Place
mask over nose and mouth and breathe
normally. Continue to use the mask until
otherwise directed by a crew member.
3. ADJUSTING THE MASK
The oxygen mask has an adjustable head
strap to provide a comfortable fit. If
mask is to tight, hold mask in position
and pull gently on headband with free
hand. If mask is to loose, pull tabs
where headband connects to oxygen
mask.
